key_findings: OSF FLoRA reproduction (node qk9v3, DOI 10.3982/ECTA10813) was located and its files downloaded: 10 auxiliary .dta explanatory files, 10 .do scripts, published-table XMLs (Table3-7), bushel claims, transparency trail, and PBR/ADR sheets.

The central dataset used by EVERY headline table, USIOrelatedparty.dta (containing the dependent variable imp_intrafirm = intrafirm import share and the tot_imp weights), is NOT present in the OSF Data component, and the Table2/3/5/7 .do files are absent from the Analysis component. The core regression therefore cannot be independently re-run from the shared package.

USIOrelatedparty.dta is derived from confidential U.S. Census Related Party Trade data; the author-hosted copy (scholar.harvard.edu) is unreachable from this environment (HTTP 403/503), it is not archived in the Wayback Machine (CDX: no captures), and no public mirror exists. The dependent variable file is thus unobtainable here, blocking independent re-computation of headline coefficients.

Published headline values (confirmed in Table3.xml) match the bushel claims exactly for the focal test: Table III benchmark (eq. 32), DUse_TUse x 1(Elas<Median) Beta_1 = -0.196 [0.071]; DUse_TUse x 1(Elas>Median) Beta_2 = 0.171 [0.067]; N = 2,783.

Verified from the shared auxiliary data that the sequential complements/substitutes median-split indicators are internally consistent: w1M1sigma is exactly the below-median indicator of w1sigma (1.00 below / 0.00 above; median = 7.60) and w1M2sigma the above-median indicator, mutually exclusive with no overlap.

Found a data-hygiene inconsistency in the shipped downstreamness.dta: the precomputed interaction columns (M1duse_tuse, M2duse_tuse, etc.) do NOT equal duse_tuse x (median-split sigma indicator) (only ~23% of rows match); the .do scripts recompute these interactions on the fly, so headline results are likely unaffected, but the shipped columns are stale.

The human FLoRA transparency trail (analyst A. Szabelska, RR 28m96) documents that, given USIOrelatedparty.dta downloaded from the author site, tables 3-7 reproduced EXACTLY after manual code fixes (focal OLS coef -0.196, N=2783); final audit CSV records values_match=Yes but repro_possible=No, without explanatory note.

Code is not push-button: hardcoded author working directories, `set memory 400m`, `# delimit ;` semicolon syntax (removed for Stata 14), multi-line commands, and dependency on external outreg2/areg packages required manual intervention before reproduction.
notes: Grade NODATA: the headline OLS coefficients could not be independently re-computed because USIOrelatedparty.dta (dependent variable + weights) is missing from the OSF package and unobtainable in this environment (confidential Census-derived; author site blocked; no mirror/no wayback capture). This agrees with the human FLoRA verdict of 'computational issues': the shared reproduction is functionally incomplete and not push-button. Corroborating evidence is strong - published numbers match the claims, the median-split logic verifies, and the human trail shows exact reproduction given the full author data - but no headline number was independently re-computed here. No numbers were fabricated. The author-site replication ZIP was also unreachable; only the OSF materials were analyzed.
